verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचपश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहेसर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O divine one, I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of distinct beings, Brahma seated on the lotus, Shiva, all the sages, and all the radiant serpents.
verses.angle: Arjuna sees the whole divine order
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form. Now he looks again and names exactly what is inside it.

body.text: Arjuna says: O divine one, I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of distinct beings, Brahma seated on the lotus, Shiva, all the sages, and all the radiant serpents. Arjuna sees the whole divine order inside Krishna's body: gods, beings of every kind, Brahma, Shiva, sages, and radiant serpents. He is looking at the structure of the cosmos. He then sees You with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, everywhere without end. He sees no beginning, middle, or end of You, O Lord of all, O cosmic form.

verses.sa: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रंपश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् । नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिंपश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥
verses.tr: I see You with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, everywhere without end. I see no beginning, middle, or end of You, O Lord of all, O cosmic form.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Listen for the word that marks a boundary breaking. This is the moment Arjuna realizes the form before him has no edges.

body.text: I see You with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, everywhere without end. I see no beginning, middle, or end of You, O Lord of all, O cosmic form. Notice the word ananta-rupam, endless-formed. Arjuna sees countless arms and faces, but the one thing that truly stops him is that this form has no beginning, middle, or end to be seen anywhere. Arjuna now asks how he can find a place to enter this endless, blazing form.

verses.sa: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं चतेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम् । पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ताद्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥
verses.tr: I see you wearing a crown, holding a mace and discus, blazing everywhere, hard to behold, and immeasurable, like fire and the sun in brilliance.
verses.angle: Tejorashim: a mass of radiance revealed
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen the formless infinite, and now he sees the details of that same form. He sees weapons, a crown, and a light he cannot stare at.

body.text: I see you wearing a crown, holding a mace and discus, blazing everywhere, hard to behold, and immeasurable, like fire and the sun in brilliance. The word tejorashim means a mass of radiance. Arjuna does not just see a man; he sees a burning, armed, crowned being whose light is too much for the eyes to hold. Arjuna now names the very form he has just seen, calling Krishna the imperishable supreme reality.

verses.sa: त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यंत्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् । त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्तासनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ॥
verses.tr: You are the imperishable supreme reality, the highest support of this world, the guardian of eternal dharma, and the eternal person.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Carrying on from the blinding light, Arjuna now tries to name what he is seeing.

body.text: You are the imperishable supreme reality, the highest support of this world, the guardian of eternal dharma, and the eternal person. Arjuna calls him the guardian of eternal dharma. By placing this name on the terrifying form, Arjuna names what he sees as the source of all order. He goes on to name the form as the endless person with infinite arms and blazing mouths.

verses.sa: अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्यमनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम् । पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम्स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ॥
verses.tr: I see you as beginningless, middleless, and endless; of infinite power, with infinite arms, with eyes like the moon and the sun, with mouths blazing like fire, and scorching this world with your own radiance.
verses.angle: Eyes of the sun and moon
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is staring at a form that breaks his ordinary sight. Listen for the first words that name what he sees.

body.text: I see you as beginningless, middleless, and endless; of infinite power, with infinite arms, with eyes like the moon and the sun, with mouths blazing like fire, and scorching this world with your own radiance. Listen to the word shasi-sury-netram, eyes of the moon and sun. He sees the same pair that mark day and night, now fixed in one face, showing the whole world contained in a single glance. Arjuna sees countless mouths blazing like fire, and the world burns in the light of his radiance. He speaks again.

verses.sa: द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हिव्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः । दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदंलोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ॥
verses.tr: The space between heaven and earth and all directions are filled by You alone. Seeing Your wondrous and fierce form, the three worlds tremble, O great one.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna keeps staring at the cosmic form. Listen for the word that shows this vision reaches every corner of existence.

body.text: The space between heaven and earth and all directions are filled by You alone. Seeing Your wondrous and fierce form, the three worlds tremble, O great one. The word lokatrayam, the three worlds, literally means heaven, earth, and the space between. It shows the form is total, filling every place that exists. Arjuna now watches the beings inside that form react, some with fear and some with praise.

verses.sa: अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घाः विशन्तिकेचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति । स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाःस्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः ॥
verses.tr: The hosts of the radiant beings enter into you. Some, frightened, join their palms and sing your names and qualities. Great seers and perfected beings praise you with abundant hymns, saying, “May all be well.”
verses.angle: Even the highest beings bow when the vast form appears.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is looking at Krishna's cosmic form, and now he points to the gods themselves. Listen for how they react.

body.text: The hosts of the radiant beings enter into you. Some, frightened, join their palms and sing your names and qualities. Great seers and perfected beings praise you with abundant hymns, saying, “May all be well.” Some gods, called surasanghah, enter into Krishna's form. Others are frightened, fold their palms, and praise him, while great seers and perfected beings sing hymns saying, 'May all be well.' Arjuna now names the Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, and Maruts, all gazing in wonder at the cosmic form.

verses.sa: रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्याविश्वेऽश्िवनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च । गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घावीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे ॥
verses.tr: The eleven Rudras, the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the twelve Sadhyas, the Visvedevas, the two Ashvins, the forty-nine Maruts, the ancestors, and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas all gaze at you in wonder.
verses.angle: All classes of beings are astonished
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is still staring at the cosmic form. Listen to every class of being he names, and notice who is looking and who is not.

body.text: The eleven Rudras, the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the twelve Sadhyas, the Visvedevas, the two Ashvins, the forty-nine Maruts, the ancestors, and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas all gaze at you in wonder. The word vispmitah means astonished. Even the highest beings, from Rudras to Asuras, are left staring in wonder at Krishna, unable to look away. Arjuna then admits that he himself is shaken by the many mouths and terrible fangs he sees in the vision.

verses.sa: रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रंमहाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् । बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालंदृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम् ॥
verses.tr: O mighty-armed one, seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and terrible fangs, all beings are shaken, and so am I.
verses.angle: Arjuna is shaken, just like all beings
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: The sight is so vast it shakes everyone, including the warrior himself. Listen to how he admits his own fear.

body.text: O mighty-armed one, seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and terrible fangs, all beings are shaken, and so am I. Arjuna does not hide his trembling. He says that all beings are shaken by the sight, and so is he. He names the many mouths, eyes, and terrible fangs to show why. Arjuna continues, saying he cannot find steadiness or peace, and asks to see Krishna's gentle form again.

verses.sa: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णंव्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् । दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्माधृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥
verses.tr: O Vishnu, seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colors, with mouths spread wide and bright, vast eyes, my inner being is shaken. I cannot find steadiness or peace.
verses.angle: Vishnu, the cosmic preserver, now the source of dread
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna asked to see the universe, but the sight has shaken his inner being. Listen for the word that names the power he thought would save him.

body.text: O Vishnu, seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colors, with mouths spread wide and bright, vast eyes, my inner being is shaken. I cannot find steadiness or peace. Arjuna calls out to Vishnu, the preserver of the cosmos. Yet the sky-touching blaze he sees does not bring him comfort. Instead, it takes away his steadiness and peace. He admits he cannot find peace, and then he asks for grace to steady himself again.

verses.sa: दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानिदृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि । दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्मप्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
verses.tr: Seeing your flaming, terrible mouths with their fangs, I can no longer find directions or peace. Be gracious, Lord of the divine beings, dwelling place of the world.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stares into the cosmic form and loses his bearings. Listen to what he sees and what he asks for.

body.text: Seeing your flaming, terrible mouths with their fangs, I can no longer find directions or peace. Be gracious, Lord of the divine beings, dwelling place of the world. Arjuna names two things he has lost, direction and peace, before he asks for grace. He then names the warriors rushing into the mouths, crushed between the teeth.

verses.sa: अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राःसर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः । भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथाऽसौसहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः ॥
verses.tr: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and all the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with the hosts of kings and our own chief warriors, are rushing into your fearful mouths. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Listen to one name that cuts through the ranks of heroes. See how Arjuna names the greatest fighters and places them inside a cosmic mouth.

body.text: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and all the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with the hosts of kings and our own chief warriors, are rushing into your fearful mouths. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads. Notice one name, sutaputrah, the charioteer's son. It is Karna, and Arjuna places him among those already rushing into the mouths of the cosmic form. Arjuna sees the sons of Dhritarashtra and our own chief warriors all rushing into your mouths.

prev.title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
